details: Circle Internet Group, issuer of the USDC stablecoin, has received final approval from the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to establish a federally supervised national trust bank. This approval allows Circle to offer digital asset custody services under direct federal oversight and could eventually lead to OCC-supervised management of USDC reserves. This development is seen as a significant step towards integrating the crypto sector into traditional finance.
title: Circle Gains Federal Trust Bank Charter, Boosting Institutional Adoption

details: A four-year ban on a U.S. central bank digital currency (CBDC) has automatically taken effect after President Donald Trump declined to sign or veto a housing bill containing the provision. This policy shift indicates a potential delay in the development and implementation of a digital dollar in the U.S.
title: U.S. Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) Faces Four-Year Ban

details: Renewed uncertainty from a potential escalation of conflict in the Middle East has weakened short-term demand in the cryptocurrency market. This geopolitical event has increased the appeal of safe-haven markets like bonds, diverting interest from risk assets such as cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin ETFs, which had seen positive inflows earlier in the month, recorded outflows on July 8 due to these rising concerns.
title: Geopolitical Tensions in Middle East Dampen Risk Appetite for Crypto

details: Spot Bitcoin and Ethereum exchange-traded funds (ETFs) experienced positive inflows in the week ending July 10, marking an end to eight consecutive weeks of net outflows. Bitcoin funds attracted $197.40 million, while Ethereum funds saw $84.42 million in inflows. This reversal followed a period where billions had been drained from these products since mid-May.
title: Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs See First Positive Inflows in Eight Weeks
